title: Duel Decks: Blessed vs. Cursed: card flavor text

entities.name: Innistrad
entities.description: The plane where these cards are set, home to cathars, ghouls, skaabs, and vampires.

entities.name: Avacyn
entities.description: The angel whose return the Host sings of.

entities.name: Oath of Avacyn
entities.description: An in-world writing quoted in flavor text.

entities.name: Mikaeus, the Lunarch
entities.description: A religious leader who urges remembrance of ancestors.

entities.name: Thalia, Knight-Cathar
entities.description: A cathar who speaks against skaabs.

entities.name: Cathars
entities.description: Holy warriors who fight skaabs and burned vampire estates.

entities.name: Ekka
entities.description: A shopkeeper of Hanweir saved by gryffs from ghouls.

entities.name: Hanweir
entities.description: A town on Innistrad.

entities.name: Sved
entities.description: A fisherman of Nephalia who warns about the ghost-tide.

entities.name: Nephalia
entities.description: A coastal province of Innistrad.

entities.name: Tamiyo
entities.description: A researcher whose writings connect Markov Manor to cryptoliths.

entities.name: Markov Manor
entities.description: A manor whose fate is connected to the cryptoliths.

entities.name: Cryptoliths
entities.description: Stone structures Tamiyo believed connected to the fate of Markov Manor.

entities.name: Jenrik
entities.description: The owner of a tower served by geists of those who tried to enter uninvited.

entities.name: Jenrik's tower
entities.description: A tower served by those who sought to enter it uninvited.

entities.name: Thraben
entities.description: A city of Innistrad offering relative safety.

entities.name: Ludevic
entities.description: A necro-alchemist who builds skaabs.

entities.name: Stitcher Geralf
entities.description: A stitcher who praises the best skaabs.

entities.name: Sorin Markov
entities.description: A vampire who speaks of sacrifices for the good of Innistrad.

entities.name: Enslow
entities.description: A ghoulcaller of Nephalia.

entities.name: Jadar
entities.description: A ghoulcaller of Nephalia who sends ghouls to feast.

entities.name: Liliana Vess
entities.description: A necromancer who boasts of her real power over Innistrad's ghoulcallers.

entities.name: Bishop Cawle of Elgaud
entities.description: A bishop who comments on the Harvester of Souls.

entities.name: Olivia Voldaren
entities.description: An ancient vampire who has outlasted a hundred mortal families.

entities.name: Marella
entities.description: A mother hosting a ball for her daughter's suitors.

entities.name: The Host
entities.description: Angels who sing of Avacyn's return.

entities.name: Ghost-tide
entities.description: A phenomenon in Nephalia heralded by ravens.

events.summary: Gryffs rescue Ekka after ghouls smash the door of her shop in Hanweir.
events.quote: "Ghouls smashed the door, but I heard the call of the gryffs and knew we were saved."

events.summary: Cathars kill Ludevic's skaabs; he responds by building flying skaabs.
events.quote: "The cathars killed my skaabs down below. Let's see how high their swords can reach."

events.summary: Cathars burned vampire estates, driving some vampires to corpse trading.
events.quote: Some vampires resorted to corpse trading after cathars burned their estates and drove them from their ancestral feeding grounds.

events.summary: At Marella's ball, her daughter disappears with a handsome stranger.
events.quote: The ball had attracted so many suitors for her daughter, including that handsome stranger.

events.summary: Olivia Voldaren watches a captured slayer's last crisis of faith.
events.quote: I want to watch this so-called slayer's last crisis of faith.

relations.quote: "The cathars killed my skaabs down below.
Jenrik's tower is served by those who once sought to enter it uninvited.
The Host sings of Avacyn's return without a single verse about its own suffering.

relations.note: Tamiyo believes its fate is connected to the cryptoliths
relations.quote: 'I'm certain that the fate of Markov Manor is connected to these cryptoliths . . .'
